traceability.notes:
The story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS is fully implemented.
All acceptance criteria are satisfied: - Core Functionality & Pattern Config (REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG): valid-annotation-format accepts both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) regex pattern options, resolved via resolveOptions and used as storyPattern/reqPattern in the rule. - Backward Compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT): When no patterns are configured, the rule uses getDefaultStoryPattern/getDefaultReqPattern and their examples. When invalid regexes are configured, resolvePattern records an error and returns defaults, so previous behavior is preserved. - Pattern Validation (REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION): resolvePattern instantiates new RegExp inside try/catch; failures are recorded via buildInvalidRegexError and surfaced through meta.messages.invalidRuleConfiguration in the rule’s Program handler, without stopping validation. - Error Messages & Examples (REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES): resolveExample chooses nested examples over flat, and both over defaults. buildStoryErrorMessage/buildReqErrorMessage use ResolvedAnnotationOptions.storyExample/reqExample, so custom storyPathExample and requirementIdExample (or nested equivalents) appear in diagnostics. Tests verify both basic use and nested-over-flat precedence. - Quality & Schema (REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION): getRuleSchema defines a strict JSON schema for story/req nested objects plus flat shorthand fields and forbids additionalProperties, following ESLint rule schema best practices. - Integration/Consistency: valid-annotation-format’s configurable patterns are independent of, but compatible with, valid-story-reference’s storyDirectories configuration. Both rules are present and correctly configured in the plugin’s exported configs, and valid-story-reference’s schema is tested in tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts, aligning with the story’s consistency requirement. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents the nested and flat configuration options, gives concrete examples aligned with the story (different directory structures, requirement prefixes, and file formats), and describes invalid-regex behavior. - Tests: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts is explicitly tagged for this story and contains comprehensive tests covering nested/flat patterns, precedence, invalid regex handling and fallback, and custom examples in error messages, providing strong automated verification of all behaviors described in the story.
Based on this concrete evidence across implementation, schema, tests, and documentation, the specification in docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md is fully met.
